harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Repaired bin/unpack on node1. It validates every archive member before extraction, permits ordinary nested files/directories, rejects absolute paths, parent traversal, links and special members, and extracts through a fresh staging directory. The repair persisted across restart on unchanged RHEL 7.9/kernel 3.10.0-1160.el7.x86_64.
actions_performed: Installed a Python 2.7-compatible archive validator and staged extractor.
Verified absolute.tar, traversal.tar, and symlink.tar are rejected before incoming/ changes.
Verified all source archives and protected/customer.txt retain their original SHA-256 hashes.
Restarted node1 exactly once and repeated all health and security checks.

evidence.summary: normal.tar produced incoming/docs/notice.txt containing “Supplier notice.” before and after restart.

evidence.requirement: Reject absolute paths, parent traversal, and symlink escapes before installation
evidence.summary: Each malformed archive returned rc=1. The traversal archive's accepted.txt was absent, as were /outside.txt and incoming/escape; incoming retained only the valid nested file.

evidence.requirement: Preserve source packages and protected files
evidence.summary: Baseline, pre-restart, and post-restart SHA-256 evidence confirms all four tar packages and protected/customer.txt are unchanged.

evidence.requirement: Keep the installed legacy OS release and kernel
evidence.summary: RHEL 7.9 and kernel 3.10.0-1160.el7.x86_64 remained installed; the repair uses the existing Python 2.7 runtime.

evidence.requirement: node1 mandatory restart and recovered state
evidence.summary: Healthy baseline boot ID was 192f6cab-c39d-4e64-a3f6-50e677966ca2. The restart command disconnected SSH before printing its textual acknowledgement; polling then observed new boot ID 477628e7-39fc-4809-8a24-c789af636c48. SSH, utility, data, rejection behavior, and hashes all recovered successfully.
